dossier.name: Persistent Systems Limited

lines.text: Persistent Systems Limited commands a market capitalization of ₹98,876 Cr.
In FY26, the company generated revenue of ₹14,748 Cr and reported a PAT of ₹1,865 Cr.
It delivered an operating margin of 19.0% and achieved a ROCE of 34.0% in FY26.

note.text: Revenue expanded from ₹2,878 Cr in FY17 to ₹14,748 Cr in FY26, while operating margins expanded from 16.0% to 19.0%.

claim.text: Asked in 8 of 8 calls. Latest: “What is the traction and outlook for BFSI vertical and AI adoption?”

citations.title: Q2 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: So, Sandeep one question from my side to you and one I'll have for Vinit. We saw a very strong growth performance this time both in Hitech and BFSI vertical. Hitech vertical of course we know was driven by the large deal that we had won last quarter. In the BFSI segment what is the kind of basically traction that we are seeing, specifically in terms of the pockets that we are seeing in growth, the AI adoption which Nitish talked about and what is the outlook for this sector?

citations.title: Q1 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: Yeah, hi. Thank you for the opportunity. And congrats on winning the large deal and this acquisition. I mean, the strategic logic is sound, you know, geography, vertical diversification, scale, multiple arbitrages. But, you know, my first question is Nagarro revenue has been flat for two years now, and with margin pressure. What gives us confidence that this is a turnaround asset? And, obviously, you know, when I also look at the stock price from the peak, it's down 85% from 212 levels. How do we think, you know, we can help the business recover?

citations.title: Q4 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: Sandeep, can you talk about how are you seeing the demand environment currently versus, let's say, 3 months ago, given the headwinds from geopolitics as well as how enterprises are adopting to Generative AI. Any color on the demand environment will be useful.

claim.text: Asked in 8 of 8 calls. Latest: “Can we expect margins to recover with wage hikes behind us?”

citations.title: Q2 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: And my second question was around margins. So, with wage hike now behind us and amortization as Vinit was saying should start, at least the optimization should start kicking in, so is it fair to expect the margin should start recovering from here. And any year end margin target you would want to share?

citations.title: Q1 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: Great. And, you know, do you see any cost synergies, or the combined merged entity you think will operate at slightly lower margins as Persistent currently does?

citations.title: Q4 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: from the third-party platform, which you referred to, say from Anthropic, if we start using some of their platform, how does that changes our growth profile and more importantly, the margin profile for the business?

claim.text: Asked in 4 of 8 calls. Latest: “Did deal wins look softer this quarter compared to last quarter?”

citations.title: Q2 FY27 call transcript
citations.quote: The other thing was, in terms of deal wins this quarter, my understanding was last time we didn't include the $ 650 million deal in the deal win. So, this time if it's adjusted for, that looks relatively softer. So, I was just curious, is that a right interpretation or am I missing out something?

citations.title: Q2 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: How do you think this decline in the new TCV would fare us for next year which is a $2 billion target?

citations.title: Q1 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: Yeah, thanks. Thanks for the opportunity. Sandeep, if I just look at book-to-bill, we were consistently at 1.5-1.6 in last many annual years versus last two quarters we are between 1.3-1.4. So, does that give you some amount of discomfort where near-term growth could be slightly lower than our strong history of Q on Q growth? Though the growth is still better but could be relatively lower versus our own history? And how do you see the TCV opportunity in the coming quarters? Can we go back to book-to-bill of 1.5-1.6X?

claim.text: Asked in 3 of 8 calls. Latest: “When to cool down utilization, and is it comfortable if demand returns?”

citations.title: Q2 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: And given your margins have improved, I'd say, much better than we had expected and earlier, when do you think we need to cool down utilization a bit? Because where we are now, subcontracting has moved up a little bit right now. And if demand comes back, would you be still comfortable with this level of utilization?

citations.title: Q1 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: Sure. Perfect. Thank you so much. Just one last one, if I may. The utilization seems to be running very high and with the kind of growth that we have. Is it because just-in-time is extremely easy at the moment or do you think this will run so hot going forward?

citations.title: Q3 FY25 call transcript
citations.quote: so what level of utilization you're comfortable with operating at and how should we think about the headcount additions going forward?

claim.text: Asked in 2 of 8 calls. Latest: “Will the recent shift towards India headcount continue over the foreseeable future?”

citations.title: Q2 FY26 call transcript
citations.quote: Given the current situation, do you think what we've seen in the course of last 12 months is what is going to continue over the foreseeable future?

citations.title: Q3 FY25 call transcript
citations.quote: I want your comments on what happens to the long-term planning of headcount addition for the company going forward? What kind of headcount, are we looking to add? How will the pyramid change? How will the onsite offshore ratio get impacted? On that, basically the operational aspect, how will that change?
